A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NaviAgent and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Renamed components and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated ToolBench and API-Bank evaluations, fine-tuning results, component analyses, and graph link-prediction scores.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional real-world API tests, static-graph comparisons, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix B.2 explicitly reports parallelizing searches for different target APIs to eliminate the original serial-loop bottleneck, a limited execution-procedure revision. The four-action agent, HGT architecture, training losses, and graph-evolution mechanisms remain substantively unchanged despite renaming.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates generated tasks in simulated ToolBench and API-Bank environments. v2 retains these and adds real-world evaluation using 50 RapidAPI APIs across seven domains (Appendix F.1). This introduces an actual-service testing environment beyond the earlier simulation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Static+A, a static graph with Alpha-Beta pruning, to the ToolBench and API-Bank comparisons. The existing Decider, D+N(Alpha), and D+N(Heur) configurations correspond to Base, Dynamic+A, and Dynamic+H. ReAct, ToolLLM, and α-UMI remain the external baselines.

E3.justification: The reported heuristic-search temperature changes from 300 to 200 and population size from 40 to 20. Added evaluations introduce 60 real-API queries balanced across three difficulty levels, a static-graph control, and runtime measured in seconds. Existing simulated dataset counts, difficulty definitions, primary metrics, and fine-tuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: The graph/no-graph and search-strategy analyses are expanded with static-versus-dynamic graph comparisons across both benchmarks, directly testing the contribution of graph evolution. Appendix F.2 adds runtime analysis exposing the cost of heuristic search. The three appendix cases largely remain, with Case 1's initial candidate list revised from three APIs to two.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results do not introduce uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Many benchmark and ablation entries are revised, and static-graph, real-API, and runtime results are added. Table 1's overall NaviAgent TSR changes from 36.4/44.9/55.5 to 35.8/45.4/55.2 for Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B, and Deepseek-V3. These accompany changed search settings and should not be treated as same-setting gains or losses. Link-prediction results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, HGT equations, loss functions, search scoring functions, and evolution equations are retained. The full cross-entropy and adaptive-margin objectives move from v1 Appendix B.2 into v2 Section 3.2.2; this does not introduce new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of scalable, graph-guided bilevel tool orchestration remains. v2 adds an explicit 'first' bilevel-framework claim and emphasizes co-evolution of the graph and decision policy. It also retreats from v1's claimed novel heuristic search by presenting the search strategies as representative adaptations.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of static-versus-dynamic graph results and identifies heuristic-search runtime as an optimization target. Its conclusion compresses the interface and dynamic-environment limitations, while replacing v1's explicit single-agent and multimodal-generalization limitation with a proposed extension to multi-agent collaboration.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies tree-structured textual serialization of retrieved subgraphs and documents parallel search with revised temperature and population settings. The detailed fine-tuning hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and inference/evaluation prompts remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds ToolGen, Learning Evolving Tools for Large Language Models, Tool-Planner, and From Exploration to Mastery, while removing several survey and cold-start references. It reframes prior approaches as structured but static or adaptive but unstructured. Most of Section 2 and the central graph-planning positioning remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Component terminology changes throughout, and the method narrative is reorganized around task planning and tool-world navigation. Full graph losses move into the main text, search details are concentrated in the appendix, and limitations are integrated into the conclusion.

P2.justification: v2 introduces a comparative workflow Figure 1 and reorganizes the earlier graph/evolution artwork into Figure 2, replacing the previous main-text architecture and health-case presentation. Ablation tables gain static-graph rows, two new tables display real-API and runtime results, and plots and appendix code blocks are restyled and relocated.

improvement.justification: Real-API validation, static-graph controls, and runtime analysis address important gaps in v1. However, v2 introduces internally inconsistent API-Bank aggregates: the Deepseek-V3 Alpha variant retains difficulty-level TCRs of 99.9, 98.9, and 99.1, but its overall TCR changes from 99.1 in v1 Table 5 to 96.9 in v2 Table 7, below every constituent rate. The added evidence benefits the paper, while these reporting inconsistencies undermine reliability; the PDFs do not establish a clear net quality direction.
